---
title: "Options — Review"
---

## Essential Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Option** | Right (not obligation) to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price (*strike* $K$) until *maturity* $T$ |
| **Call** | Right to **buy** at strike $K$ |
| **Put** | Right to **sell** at strike $K$ |
| **Premium** | Price of the option (cost of insurance) |
| **European** | Exercise **only at** $T$ |
| **American** | Exercise **at any time** until $T$ |

---

## The 4 Positions

| Position | Pays | Receives | Max Loss | Max Gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Long call** | Premium $c$ | — | $c$ | Unlimited |
| **Short call** | — | Premium $c$ | **Unlimited** ⚠️ | $c$ |
| **Long put** | Premium $p$ | — | $p$ | $K - p$ |
| **Short put** | — | Premium $p$ | $K - p$ | $p$ |

::: {.callout-warning title="Pitfall"}
The **short call** is the only position with **theoretically unlimited** loss.
:::

---

## Payoffs at Maturity

| Position | Payoff |
|---|---|
| Long call | $\max(S_T - K,\ 0)$ |
| Short call | $-\max(S_T - K,\ 0)$ |
| Long put | $\max(K - S_T,\ 0)$ |
| Short put | $-\max(K - S_T,\ 0)$ |

**Profit = Payoff − Premium**

---

## Moneyness

| State | Call | Put |
|---|---|---|
| **In the money (ITM)** | $S_0 > K$ | $S_0 < K$ |
| **At the money (ATM)** | $S_0 = K$ | $S_0 = K$ |
| **Out of the money (OTM)** | $S_0 < K$ | $S_0 > K$ |

---

## Variables Influencing the Price

| Variable | ↑ Call | ↑ Put |
|---|---|---|
| Current price $S_0$ ↑ | ↑ | ↓ |
| Strike $K$ ↑ | ↓ | ↑ |
| Maturity $T$ ↑ | ↑ | ↑ |
| Volatility $\sigma$ ↑ | ↑ | ↑ |
| Rate $r$ ↑ | ↑ | ↓ |
| Dividend ↑ | ↓ | ↑ |

::: {.callout-tip title="Key takeaway"}
Volatility $\sigma$ increases the value of **both types** of options.
:::

---

## Price Bounds (No-Arbitrage)

$$S_0 - Ke^{-rT} \leq c \leq S_0$$

$$Ke^{-rT} - S_0 \leq p \leq K$$

**Discounting reminder :** $p_0 = p_T \cdot e^{-rT}$

---

## Put-Call Parity

$$\boxed{c + Ke^{-rT} = p + S_0}$$

- No-arbitrage equilibrium condition
- Allows synthesizing one instrument from the other three
- **Long put + asset = call-like** (illustrates parity)

---

## Key Strategies

| Strategy | Construction | Expectation |
|---|---|---|
| **Bull spread (calls)** | Long call $K_1$ + Short call $K_2$, $K_2 > K_1$ | Moderate rise |
| **Bull spread (puts)** | Long put $K_1$ + Short put $K_2$, $K_2 > K_1$ | Moderate rise |
| **Long butterfly** | Long $K_1$ + 2 Short $K_2$ + Long $K_3$ | Low volatility, stability |
| **Protective put** | Long asset + Long put | Protection against decline |

---

## Pricing — Binomial Tree

**1-step structure :**

- $S_0 \cdot u$ (up) with probability $p$
- $S_0 \cdot d$ (down) with probability $1-p$, $u = 1/d$

**Hedge delta :**

$$\Delta = \frac{f_u - f_d}{S_0 u - S_0 d}$$

**Risk-Neutral Probability :**

$$p = \frac{e^{rT} - d}{u - d}$$

**Option price :**

$$\boxed{f = e^{-rT}\left[p \cdot f_u + (1-p) \cdot f_d\right]}$$

**Calibration :**

$$u = e^{\sigma\sqrt{T}}, \quad d = e^{-\sigma\sqrt{T}}$$

::: {.callout-warning title="Complexity"}
$n$ steps → $2^n$ paths. At 30 steps : $\approx 10^9$ paths → memory intensive.
:::

---

## Pricing — Black-Scholes (BS)

**Call :**

$$c = S_0 N(d_1) - Ke^{-rT} N(d_2)$$

**Put :**

$$p = Ke^{-rT} N(-d_2) - S_0 N(-d_1)$$

**With :**

$$d_1 = \frac{\ln(S_0/K) + (r + \sigma^2/2)T}{\sigma\sqrt{T}}, \quad d_2 = d_1 - \sigma\sqrt{T}$$

$N(x)$ = standard normal cumulative distribution function $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$

| BS Assumption | Reality |
|---|---|
| $\sigma$ constant | Varies with $K$ and $T$ |
| Log-normal returns | Fat tails |

---

## Binomial vs Black-Scholes

| Criterion | Binomial | Black-Scholes |
|---|---|---|
| Option type | Vanilla **and** exotic | Vanilla only |
| Formula | Numerical / recursive | Closed-form analytical |
| Convergence | → BS as $n \to \infty$ | Reference |
| Complexity | Exponential in $n$ | Instantaneous |

---

## Implied Volatility & Smile

- **Implied Volatility** : $\sigma$ extracted from BS by fixing the market price.
- Theoretically constant per BS → **in practice : no**.
- **Smile** : implied $\sigma$ higher for deeply OTM or ITM options.
- **Volatility surface** : smile as a function of $K$ **and** $T$.

::: {.callout-warning title="Pitfall"}
The volatility smile is proof that BS is a **model**, not reality. Never forget its limits.
:::

---

## Reference Numerical Example

**Data :** $S_0 = 20$, $K = 21$, $T = 3/12$, $u = 1.1$, $d = 0.909$, $r = 12\%$

| Calculation | Value |
|---|---|
| $f_u = \max(22-21, 0)$ | $1$ USD |
| $f_d = \max(18.2-21, 0)$ | $0$ USD |
| $p = (e^{0.03} - 0.909) / 0.191$ | $\approx 0.636$ |
| $f = e^{-0.03}(0.636 \times 1)$ | $\approx 0.617$ USD |
| $\Delta = 1/(22-18.2)$ | $\approx 0.262$ |
| BS : $c$ | $\approx 0.593$ USD |
